terms.gloss: lodging, a place to stay; also hospitality
evidence: Cic. Att. 14.2.4: Pīliae parātum est hospitium
terms.comment: First hospitality and the bond between host and guest; then the place where a guest is put up, a lodging or guest room, or an inn (Lewis & Short). hospitiō excipere, to put someone up (Hor. S. 1.5.2); in hospitia dīvidere, to billet soldiers (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an inn, a lodging on the road
terms.comment: A place to break a journey, paid for; see hotel. The diminutive dēversōriolum is a small lodging (Cic. Att. 14.8, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a stay; (after Augustus) a lodging, night quarters
terms.comment: In Cicero “a stay, staying on”; a dwelling or a night’s quarters only from the Augustan period on (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Pīliae parātum est hospitium, sed vellem Atticam
phrases.english: a room is ready for Pilia, but I wish you would bring Attica too

phrases.latin: ex vītā ita discēdō tamquam ex hospitiō, nōn tamquam ē domō
phrases.english: I leave life as one leaves a lodging, not as one leaves home

sources: Lewis & Short: hospitium · Lewis & Short: deversorius · Lewis & Short: mansio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 268.
